title: Charlotte FC plans to sign French winger Allan Saint-Maximin, sources say
content:
Charlotte FC is finalizing a deal to sign French winger Allan Saint-Maximin, sources briefed on the situation but not authorized to speak publicly tell The Athletic.

Saint-Maximin will join on a free transfer and occupy a designated player slot for Charlotte. Fabrizio Romano first reported the deal.

The 29-year-old winger spent the past few months with Lens, where he had three goals and three assists in 403 minutes. He abruptly left Mexican giants Club America this winter by mutual consent, alleging racial abuse directed at his children.

Saint-Maximin surprised the soccer world when he went to Mexico in August. He made 16 appearances in Mexico.

The move was only made possible for Charlotte following the departure of Wilfried Zaha, who is now a free agent. Saint-Maximin will occupy the DP spot Zaha’s departure opened. Pep Biel and Liel Abada are the club’s other two DPs.

Saint-Maximin previously featured for Newcastle, Al-Ahli, Fenerbahce, Monaco and more in a well-traveled career. He spent four seasons in England with Newcastle after a transfer worth north of $20 million, scoring 13 goals across 124 appearances, after a transfer from Nice in France.

Charlotte sit sixth in the Eastern Conference with 21 points after 15 matches. MLS is currently on a World Cup break and will resume in mid-July.
